version.changelog:
## v1.1.0
Version bump. Updated homepage URL. Part of the v1.1.0 release adding migration compatibility matrix to prisma-migrate.

llm.summary: The skill is coherent for Prisma Access API management, but it gives an agent high-impact curl-based authority to change and push security configuration with limited built-in safeguards.

dimensions.detail: SCM_CLIENT_ID, SCM_CLIENT_SECRET, and SCM_TSG_ID are proportionate for SCM API use, but they are sensitive credentials and the broad curl permission is wider than the documented Palo Alto endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill with no bundled executable scripts, installers, package dependencies, persistence hooks, or obfuscated code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill allows Bash(curl *) and says to execute the requested operation; write, delete, and candidate push examples are present, while confirmation, diff, rollback, and dependency checks are only lightly covered by advisory safety text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, local credential-store access, memory writes, scheduled tasks, privilege escalation, or system modification behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is clear and disclosed, including querying, creating, updating, and deleting Prisma Access configuration objects, but those actions can alter live security posture and connectivity.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing in a production tenant. Use least-privileged or test SCM credentials, avoid exposing the client secret or bearer token in logs, and require explicit human review plus backup or rollback planning before create, update, delete, or candidate push operations.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: live mutation capability is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the artifact under-specifies service-impact warnings, confirmation gates, rollback, and safer defaults for high-impact changes.
[E1] expected: External network transmission to Palo Alto Networks authentication and SCM API endpoints is expected for this API-management skill; no unrelated destination was found in the artifact.
[E1] unexpected: The scanner also flagged POST, PUT, DELETE, and candidate push examples; these are not evidence of exfiltration, but they do support the Review concern because they can modify or deploy security configuration without enforced guardrails.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 results, consistent with the inspected artifact showing no instruction hijacking, persistence, embedded code, remote payload execution, or tool spoofing.
